cards.claim: Final and later layers of CNNs require disproportionately higher channel counts than earlier layers to achieve optimal accuracy
cards.conditions: ImageNet classification with ResNet18 and MobileNetV2 architectures; width optimization across DMCP, AutoSlim, and MorphNet algorithms
cards.effect: Optimized networks expand final layer widths dramatically—ResNet18 from 512→1300 channels (~2.5×); MobileNetV2 from 1280→3785 channels (~3×)
cards.evidence: Empirical measurement via width optimization experiments across three state-of-the-art algorithms; visualization in Figure 5
cards.quote: We find that the later layers tend to increase a lot compared to the un-optimized ones. Concretely, in un-optimized networks, ResNet18 has 512 channels in the last layer and MobileNetV2 has 1280 channels in the last layer. In contrast, the average optimized width has 1300 channels for ResNet18 and 3785 channels for MobileNetV2.

cards.claim: Width optimization produces scale-invariant patterns within network stages; relative widths within a stage transfer reliably across different network depths
cards.conditions: Network width optimization on ImageNet; depth multipliers {1,2,3,4}; ResNet18 and MobileNetV2; all three width optimization algorithms (DMCP, AutoSlim, MorphNet)
cards.effect: ~75% width optimization overhead reduction while preserving accuracy; layer stacking strategies (stack-average-block, stack-last-block) reliably transfer patterns across depth variations
cards.evidence: Experiments in Section 4.3; Figure 4(c)-(d); empirical validation across compound projections; controlled experiments with three random seeds
cards.quote: In other words, the pattern of width multipliers across depth is scale-invariant.

cards.claim: Non-uniform narrowing across blocks without maintaining coordinated width relationships across stages causes accuracy degradation beyond isolated block-level predictions
cards.conditions: Width optimization with block-level width changes; ImageNet classification; resolution and architecture projection experiments; MorphNet, AutoSlim, and DMCP algorithms
cards.effect: MorphNet transferred from low resolution (64px) to ResNet18 shows substantial accuracy loss compared to direct optimization; demonstrates that block-structure coherence is required for maintaining accuracy
cards.evidence: Experiment in Section 4.4; Figure 7(a); comparison of optimized widths across different resolutions shown in Appendix similarity analysis; mismatch between transferred and directly-optimized architectures
cards.quote: Interestingly, we find that MorphNet had a very different optimized widths when transferred from resolution 64 for ResNet18, which leads to the worse performance for ResNet18 compared to direct optimization.
